cards.text: Hezekiah, king of Judah, is in the fourteenth year of his reign. Then Sennacherib, king of Assyria, attacks the fortified cities of Judah. Walls, gates, guards, the whole deal.

cards.question: Sennacherib king of Assyria goes after Judah's fortified cities. How many of them does he capture?

cards.text: Then the king of Assyria sends the Rabshakeh, a royal officer, out from Lachish with a great army.

cards.question: The Rabshakeh marches out of Lachish with a great army. The king of Assyria is sending him to King Hezekiah at ___.

cards.text: He stops by the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer's Field. Three of Hezekiah's men go out to meet him: Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe and Joah the recorder.

cards.question: The Rabshakeh gives the three men a message for Hezekiah from the king of Assyria. What does the message ask about first?

answers.text: What Hezekiah's confidence is based on
How much silver Hezekiah can pay
When Hezekiah will open the gates

cards.text: His very first question: "What is the basis of this confidence of yours?" That's a man standing in YOUR driveway asking what makes you think you can park there.

cards.question: The Rabshakeh says Hezekiah's claim to have a strategy and strength for war is nothing but ___ words.
Then the Rabshakeh asks, "In whom are you now trusting, that you have rebelled against me?" Which nation does he say Judah is leaning on?
The Rabshakeh has a picture for what it's like to lean on Egypt. What does he call Egypt?

answers.text: A splintered reed of a staff
A crumbling wall with no gate
A dry well with no water

cards.text: That reed, he says, will pierce the hand of anyone who leans on it, and Pharaoh is the same to all who trust in him. And if they say they trust in the LORD their God, he says Hezekiah is the one who removed the LORD's high places and altars.

cards.question: According to the Rabshakeh, Hezekiah told Judah and Jerusalem they must worship before one altar.

cards.text: Then he says, "Now, therefore, make a bargain with my master, the king of Assyria." Friend, that's the tow truck driver with your car already on the hook leaning out the window going, "So... let's work something out."

cards.question: The Rabshakeh offers Hezekiah two thousand horses. What's the catch?

answers.text: If they can put riders on them
If they pay silver for each one
If they open the city gates first

cards.text: That's somebody handing you a whole box of free puppies and then asking, real sweet, "Oh, you don't have a yard?" Then he says they can't push back even one of his master's least officers while they depend on Egypt for chariots and horsemen.

cards.question: The Rabshakeh claims the LORD Himself told him to go up against this land and destroy it.

cards.text: Then Eliakim, Shebna and Joah ask him, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, since we understand it." Not in Hebrew, they tell him.

cards.question: The three officials ask the Rabshakeh not to speak Hebrew in the hearing of the people on the ___.
The Rabshakeh agrees to switch to Aramaic for the three officials.

cards.text: The Rabshakeh says his master sent these words for the men sitting on the wall too, men he says are destined to eat their own dung and drink their own urine.
Then the Rabshakeh stands up, and friend, when the man you just asked a favor of STANDS UP, that is not a yes.

cards.question: The Rabshakeh now calls out loudly in Hebrew.

cards.text: He shouts, "Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!" And the king's words are, "Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he cannot deliver you."

cards.question: The Rabshakeh tells the people not to let Hezekiah persuade them to trust in the LORD. What does he say Hezekiah tells them about the city?

answers.text: It won't be given to the king of Assyria
Its wells will never run dry

cards.text: Then he switches from threats to a sales pitch. The king of Assyria says, "Make peace with me and come out to me."

cards.question: The Rabshakeh says if the people make peace and come out, what will every one of them get?

answers.text: To eat from his own vine and fig tree
To serve in the king of Assyria's army
To take silver from the king's treasury

cards.question: The Rabshakeh promises the people they can stay in their own land for good.

cards.text: They get all that until the king of Assyria comes and takes them away to a land like their own, a land of grain and new wine. That's the free trial, friend, and page nine of the fine print says WE'RE MOVING YOU.

Then he asks, "Has the god of any nation ever delivered his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?" He names the gods of Hamath, Arpad and Sepharvaim, and asks whether they delivered Samaria, the capital of the northern kingdom of Israel, from his hand.

cards.question: After naming all those gods, the Rabshakeh asks how the LORD can deliver Jerusalem from his hand.
After everything the Rabshakeh shouts, how do the people respond?
The people don't say a word back to the Rabshakeh, because King ___ had commanded, "Do not answer him."

cards.text: Not one word, friend, and I spent enough years in a junk drawer to know a LOUD silence when I hear one. Then Eliakim, Shebna and Joah head back to King Hezekiah.

cards.question: Eliakim, Shebna and Joah reach King Hezekiah. What do they do there?

answers.text: Urge him to surrender the city
Beg him to send for Egypt

cards.text: And all three of them come in with their clothes torn. I bet those words hit hard.
That's where we'll stop for now, friend. Keep your apron on, because this story's still got more in the oven.
